item.title: Les TPE : vers de nouveaux modèles d'affaires ?
item.content:encoded:
Marion Polge, Université de Montpellier

Isabelle Calmé, Université de Tours

Colette Fourcade, Université de Montpellier

Les très petites entreprises (TPE) restent largement sous-étudiées malgré leur importance statistique et sociale. Ce numéro interroge si elles constituent des organisations singulières au-delà de simples PME réduites. Par leur légèreté structurelle, leurs interactions intenses et leur proximité territoriale, elles développent des modes d'ajustement innovants et des dynamiques entrepreneuriales spécifiques, plus sobres et résilientes que les organisations plus établies.

Depuis 2020, les mutations systémiques – crises sanitaires, défis écologiques, numérisation – transforment profondément les TPE. Le numéro explore comment elles réinventent la performance au-delà de la croissance, adoptant des approches multiformes axées sur l'équilibre, la durabilité et l'impact local. Les nouvelles technologies créent tant des opportunités que des vulnérabilités pour ces organisations.

Appel publié par Revue internationale P M E Économie et gestion de la petite et moyenne entreprise. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Trajectoires stratégiques atypiques et diversification des profils de dirigeants de TPE : profils, motivations, rapport au travail et au risque, bifurcations de parcours
  • Redéfinition de la performance dans les TPE : indicateurs alternatifs, refus de la croissance, équilibre de vie, ancrage territorial, relations au vivant
  • TPE, écologie et raréfaction des ressources : modèles économiques frugaux, économie circulaire, décroissance choisie, entreprise régénérative, impact écologique
  • TPE et technologies : appropriation, marginalisation ou résistance face à la numérisation, à l'intelligence artificielle, à l'ubérisation ou à la plate-forme-économie
  • Formes alternatives d'organisation et d'innovation : bricolage, mutualisation, coopération, hybridation des statuts, pratiques informelles ou hybrides
  • Rôle des TPE dans les transitions sociales et territoriales : résilience locale, dynamiques d'inclusion, réponses aux crises systémiques, justice économique
  • Méthodologies et épistémologies de recherche adaptées aux TPE : recherches partenariales, approches critiques, récits de vie, ethnographie entrepreneuriale

item.title: Entrepreneurship as an Artist: Subjectivities, Contexts and Collective Dynamics
item.content:encoded:
Joëlle Bissonnette, Université du Québec à Montréal

Elen Riot, Université Paris 8

Christian Makaya, Ascencia School of Business

Céline Barredy, Université Paris Nanterre

Vanessa Serret, Université de Lorraine

This special issue examines entrepreneurial practices of artists in their activities of creation, production and dissemination. While management has long been characterized as an art due to its creative and non-iterative dimension, the relationship between artistic and managerial spheres has historically been presented as antagonistic or dichotomous. However, contemporary research reveals a growing convergence between the figures of the artist and the entrepreneur, notably through shared practices and approaches.

This convergence also reflects the growing proportion of artists becoming entrepreneurs in a socioeconomic context marked by injunctions to entrepreneurship and innovation, as well as by increasing precarity in artistic creation activities. These approaches highlight initiatives carried out by individuals often marginalized geographically or socio-culturally who mobilize cultural, social and emotional resources to create value within their communities. They also reveal the interrelations, sometimes fruitful and sometimes more harmful, between artistic creation and entrepreneurial practices and the challenges facing artistic entrepreneurs.

Appel publié par Revue internationale P M E Économie et gestion de la petite et moyenne entreprise. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Personal narratives, emotions and individual artistic trajectories and their influence on entrepreneurial practices
  • Context as a creative resource and entrepreneurial catalyst: how artists transform contextual constraints into opportunities
  • Individual-collective dynamics in artistic entrepreneurship: articulation between individual artistic expression and community engagement
  • Artistic entrepreneurship as a response to contemporary challenges: resilience strategies, alternative economic models, and sustainable development
  • Artists' relationship with their personal histories, emotions, identity negotiations and bifurcations, and their influence on entrepreneurial practices
  • How broader contextual dynamics (social, technological, environmental, political) shape and inspire artists' entrepreneurial trajectories
  • Interaction dynamics between individual artistic interests and collective action, particularly regarding tensions between personal creative expression and collaborative community engagement
  • Hybrid organizational models emerging between individual creation and collective action
  • Collaborative practices and their role in generating collective intelligence and artistic innovation
  • Governance mechanisms in artistic collectives for balancing individual expression and shared objectives
  • Role of artistic interventions in community resilience and social transformation
  • Artists' strategies for resisting and adapting to market pressures while maintaining economic viability
  • Balance between creative integrity and institutional or commercial commitments
  • Social and environmental innovations developed by artist-entrepreneurs
  • Contributions of artistic entrepreneurship to sustainable development objectives

item.title: The Double Transition of Family SMEs: Tensions, Trade-offs and Paradoxes of Sustainable and Digital Transformation
item.content:encoded:
Mohamed Ouiakoub, Université de Lorraine

Sandrine Berger-Douce, Mines Saint-Etienne

Christophe Schmitt, Université de Lorraine

Family and medium-sized enterprises (family SMEs) have distinct characteristics from both large family businesses and non-family SMEs. They are characterized by governance dominated by the family, strong emotional involvement, intergenerational transmission logic, and often more informal and conservative decision-making modes. In these organizations, the coexistence of family logic and entrepreneurial logic generates unique complexity. Family SME leaders must simultaneously pursue classical economic objectives and socio-emotional objectives linked to the owning family. Socioemotional wealth—meaning the family's affective attachment to the enterprise and willingness to preserve family heritage—strongly influences strategic decisions. Consequently, these enterprises display longer-term vision, increased aversion to losing family control, and governance centered on aligning family and organizational interests. Their small size and limited resources reinforce agility and flexibility but limit investment capacity and strategic formalization. Studies show that family SMEs tend to invest less in R&D than other SMEs while innovating more incrementally through improvements driven by family…

Appel publié par Revue internationale P M E Économie et gestion de la petite et moyenne entreprise. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How family dynamics (values, generations, roles, etc.) influence the strategies of digital and ecological transition in family SMEs
  • Specific levers and barriers to double transition in family SMEs, particularly in relation to intergenerational tensions or available resources
  • Specific tensions and paradoxes that emerge when family SMEs engage simultaneously in digitalization and sustainability
  • Management strategies and practices that family SMEs implement to manage paradoxes related to double transition
  • How business models evolve under the pressure of double transition, in a context of transmission or generational change of family SMEs
  • Effects of double transition on the sustainability and overall performance of family SMEs
  • Family governance, decision-making logics and double transition
  • Innovation, dynamic capabilities and organizational paradoxes in family SMEs facing double transition
  • Institutional contexts, local cultures and international comparisons of family SME transitions

item.title: Entrepreneurial Ecosystems & Digital Transformation
item.content:encoded:
Christina Theodoraki, IAE Aix-Marseille Université

Lynda Saoudi, Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1

Mathilde Aubry, EM Normandie

Jean-Michel Sahut, IDRAC Business School

Although the entrepreneurial ecosystem (EE) has become a crucial concept for territorial economic development, digital transformation tends to reshape the architecture of EEs and reduce spatial dependencies. This constant evolution results in the regular emergence of new actors in the digital spectrum, and fundamentally modifies the design of EEs and their boundaries, which are no longer limited to a predefined set of actors concentrated on a given territory, but to a multi-dimensional approach: 1) entrepreneurial actors, 2) entrepreneurial organizations, and 3) institutions, which can coordinate formally and informally to help generate and improve entrepreneurial activity within a specific local environment.

Appel publié par Revue internationale P M E Économie et gestion de la petite et moyenne entreprise. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Digitization of entrepreneurial ecosystems (EEs): Impact of digital transformation on EEs, new relationships and governance possibilities within entrepreneurial ecosystems
  • Relationships between ecosystems: Infra/international cooperation and coopetition
  • Digital challenges for entrepreneurial ecosystem actors: incubators, accelerators, financial actors, SMEs, etc.
  • Consequences of digitization: dehumanization, environmental impact, Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), inequalities (gender, emerging countries)
  • Behavior and strategy of stakeholders in Digital Entrepreneurial Ecosystems (DEEs): impacts on startups and SMEs
  • Relational approaches within DEEs: network structures between EEs and entrepreneurs, intra and inter DEEs
  • Inclusion and openness to social, territorial, gender and ethnocultural diversity through DEE development
  • Boundaries between EEs and DEEs for entrepreneurial stimulation
  • Conceptual proximity and diversity, overlaps between concepts? Substitution and/or complementarity?
  • Public policy issues, entrepreneurial processes and innovation practices in the context of DEEs
  • Economic models and digital transformation for SMEs and EEs
  • Interactions between digital platforms and EEs
  • Ecosystem for supporting entrepreneurs and SMEs in their digital transformation
  • Digital maturity of companies and entrepreneurial ecosystems in digital transformation
